dimension_justifications.soundness: The paired estimands, discordance arithmetic, multiplicity families, and boundaries on interpretation are specified unusually carefully, and the reported counts are internally arithmetically consistent where they can be checked. However, every central outcome is source-reported and cannot_verify from this snapshot: the claim map says cannot_verify_locally, the registry says the experiments were not rerun, and the package lacks item-level records, implementations, registrations, and analysis code. This is a decision-relevant soundness and reproducibility gap, even though it is candidly disclosed.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is understandable after close reading, with a useful five-arm definition table, intervention-estimand map, and budget forest plot. Evaluation is nevertheless obstructed by dense audit/status vocabulary, repeated chronology and budget ledgers, long captions, mixed interval conventions, and a central reveal-order table whose sign and role require footnote decoding. Internal run identifiers also conflict with the paper's anonymity statement.
dimension_justifications.contribution: A bed-local audit of scoring-protocol dependence for one masked-diffusion model and one GSM8K-MC construction is identifiable and potentially useful. Its significance is intrinsically narrow, component-level causality and transfer are disclaimed, and the snapshot's citation lock is pending with zero citations verified, so distinctness and positioning cannot_verify beyond the manuscript's assertions.

paper_summary: The submission studies how five multiple-choice scoring protocols for LLaDA-8B-Instruct on four-choice GSM8K-MC change measured accuracy. It reports a pre-registered n=400 matched-draw s_conf versus mc_uniform gap of +13.0 percentage points, a post-selected 2L/2L forward-count sensitivity with the same gap, a +9.0 point high-budget conservative read, and a fresh-pool result in which fixed left-to-right order beats s_conf on average but reverses at answer position 0. The intended conclusion is deliberately narrow: scoring protocols are not interchangeable on this bed, while actual compute parity, causal component attribution, multi-seed stability, and generalization remain unresolved. The main text fits the nine-page limit, with references beginning on page 9 and appendices on page 11; the paper uses an anonymous author line, but embedded run identifiers create a residual anonymity concern.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest contribution verifiable from the supplied objects is the explicit conceptual and accounting decomposition of scoring protocols: Table 1 distinguishes feedback, reveal schedule, scoring forwards, and adaptive selection forwards, while Table 4 states the narrow estimand supported by each comparison. The numerical effect sizes themselves remain source_reported/cannot_verify_locally because their underlying records are absent.
strengths: The abstract and conclusion consistently bound the claim to one model-dataset bed and explicitly reject unsupported readings about FLOPs, latency, dose response, causal components, and transfer.
Table 1, Table 4, and Figure 2 provide complementary views of protocol components, estimands, and the tested reference-budget curve.
The manuscript distinguishes pre-registered primary, post-selected sensitivity, exploratory, undetermined, and secondary results more candidly than is typical.
The PDF is legible, uses an anonymous author line, and respects the maximum nine main-text pages; references start on page 9 and the appendix starts on page 11.
Limitations and Appendix H explicitly acknowledge the absent item-level records, registrations, environment capture, and regeneration scripts instead of presenting the checklist as evidence.
questions: Can the authors supply the anonymous E10-E15 item-level records, registrations, analysis code, environment manifest, and one-command recomputation route so that Tables 2, 5, and 7 can be independently verified?

What single hierarchy should readers use among the matched-L primary, 2L/2L post-selected sensitivity, nmc=128 conservative read, and fresh fixed-order secondary result? The current abstract, Section 4, Section 6, and appendix ledgers distribute this hierarchy across many status labels.
Why are timestamped result paths and Trial 1895183 printed in the blind PDF when page 20 states that workflow labels, machine paths, and task identifiers are absent?
What model/tool and prompt produced Figure 1, and was generative AI used for text, code, or other figures?

issues.location: PDF Abstract and Introduction, pages 1-2; Section 3, pages 3-4; Section 4, pages 4-6; Section 6, pages 7-8; Appendix D-G, pages 14-19, especially Tables 11-14 and 19-21
issues.observed_evidence: The same four reference-budget points and their status labels are restated in the abstract, numbered introduction claims, load-bearing estimand paragraph, Section 4 prose, Figure 2, Table 2, and multiple appendix ledgers. Readers must track nominal draw match, forward-count match, high-budget conservative read, planning MDE, promotion bar, Holm family, historical Tier-25 gate, pre-registration, and post-selection before the primary story is stable.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's caution is valuable, but status-first repetition obscures the simple scientific result and makes it difficult to distinguish the single primary endpoint from sensitivity and secondary analyses. This materially lowers Presentation and risks readers attaching the wrong evidential weight to post-selected results.
issues.required_fix: Choose one explicit evidence hierarchy and state it once: primary matched-L result, post-selected forward-count sensitivity, high-budget robustness point, and separate reveal-order secondary result. Keep one compact contrast/estimand/status table in the main text, move registration chronology, MDE formulas, duplicate budget ledgers, and robustness bookkeeping to the appendix, and shorten captions to interpretation-critical facts.
issues.verification_test: Give the revised main paper to a fresh reader and require them, without consulting the appendix, to identify the primary endpoint, each sensitivity, the comparison direction, what was pre-specified versus post-selected, and the supported conclusion in under two minutes; all answers should match the single hierarchy table.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is needed; a reorganized manuscript with a single canonical endpoint hierarchy and deduplicated ledgers is sufficient.

issues.location: PDF Section 6, pages 7-8, especially Table 5 and notes on page 8, lines 378-406; Appendix Table 7, page 11
issues.observed_evidence: Table 5 mixes s_conf-rand_inject and s_conf-fixed_inject contrasts, one- and two-sided intervals, lower bounds, MDE80 values, pilot/fresh/pooled estimands, post-selection roles, and exclusion versus detection readings. The headline fixed-order win is encoded as a negative s_conf-minus-fixed delta and clarified only through footnotes d/e and the role cell; Table 7 adds construction and position reversals separately.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the central schedule result, but its direction, inferential convention, and evidential status are harder to read than the result itself. The mixed table increases the chance of reporting the wrong sign or treating heterogeneous/post-hoc rows as replications.
issues.required_fix: Split Table 5 into separate random-order and fixed-order panels or tables. Print each contrast direction in the row label, use one display interval convention per panel, place MDE and registration status in separate columns, and put the answer-position reversal next to the aggregate fixed-order row. Reserve pooled heterogeneous estimates and alternate conventions for the appendix.
issues.verification_test: Ask independent readers to state who wins each row, which rows are primary/secondary/post-hoc, which interval is displayed, and whether pools may be combined; require unanimous answers without reading footnotes.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is required; the existing reported rows need a standardized, explicitly directed presentation.

issues.observed_evidence: The citation lock status is pending_full_audit and verified_this_round is empty. The related-work section makes broad claims about scorer dependence and closest mechanism literatures, but no supplied object verifies bibliographic metadata or local sentence support.
issues.why_it_matters: Under the frozen evidence, citation correctness, closest-work coverage, and the claimed distinctness of the protocol audit cannot_verify. This materially limits confidence in Contribution and positioning without demonstrating that any citation is wrong.
issues.required_fix: Provide a reviewer-safe citation verification summary for every cited work, including primary-source metadata, the exact local claim supported, and a closest-work matrix focused on masked-diffusion multiple-choice scoring and protocol/accounting audits. Narrow any sentence whose support cannot be verified.
issues.verification_test: For every citation, match title, authors, venue/year, DOI or stable URL against a primary source and verify that the cited source supports the exact sentence; independently confirm that the closest-work matrix covers the paper's claimed gap.
issues.evidence_needed: A completed citation lock with primary-source metadata and sentence-level support notes; no outside inference should substitute for it.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics concern is evident from the frozen snapshot: the work audits a model on a math multiple-choice benchmark, reports no human-subject study or deployment, and avoids broad capability claims. Dataset licensing, model-license compliance, and the actual compute/environment footprint cannot_verify because the artifact is absent, but nothing supplied indicates a concrete ethics violation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by reviewer A14-R00-C, an isolated AI subagent, for internal pre-submission quality control. It was restricted to the frozen snapshot and did not inspect outside literature, prior reviews, repository history, author plans, score trajectories, or target scores.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A complete anonymous E10-E15 artifact that independently reproduces every central count, paired test, interval, multiplicity decision, and quantitative figure.

A substantially simplified main-text hierarchy that makes primary, sensitivity, conservative, and secondary endpoints immediately distinguishable and standardizes comparison directions and interval conventions.
Removal of internal run and trial identifiers, with anonymous bundle-local evidence IDs that resolve to submitted files.
A completed primary-source citation and local-support audit demonstrating accurate metadata and a clear gap relative to the closest masked-diffusion scoring work.

Pinned multi-seed schedule replays and a component-separating factorial ablation would raise confidence beyond the current single-realization, full-protocol comparison, although these are new experiments rather than presentation-only fixes.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Recomputed item-level records that fail to match the reported accuracies, discordant counts, pool membership, Holm families, or bootstrap intervals.
Evidence that the n=400 matched-L registration or fresh fixed-order pre-specification occurred after inspecting the relevant outcomes.
Multi-seed schedule replays that erase or reverse the reported fresh-pool schedule results without a corresponding narrowing of the claims.
A citation audit showing that the closest work already contains the same protocol/accounting audit or that key related-work claims are unsupported.
Any demonstrated link between the printed run/trial identifiers and the authors' identities or non-anonymous infrastructure.
review_limitations: No outside literature was consulted by instruction; citation accuracy, novelty, and closest-work completeness therefore cannot_verify beyond the empty pending citation lock.

The snapshot contains no raw per-item experimental records, executable method implementation, registrations, analysis scripts, environment capture, or figure-generation payloads, so all central numerical claims remain source-reported.
